# Chatwarden

> Chatwarden is free, open-source chat moderation for games: a check for every chat message (slurs from your word list, optional swearing filter), in-game reporting with evidence, player notices, and a moderator hub (one case per player by default). It moderates the chat you already have, and has an optional moderated chat box for a game with none. TypeScript for Node 22.13 or newer. Pre-release (0.2.x), Apache-2.0, provided as-is. Not a child-safety tool.

The packages are small and independent. Start with the repository README, then install `@chatwarden/core`, `@chatwarden/store-sqlite` and `@chatwarden/matcher`. For a moderator screen add `@chatwarden/hub-react` (or `@chatwarden/hub-element`) and `@chatwarden/http` for the routes it reads, and `@chatwarden/player-react` for what players see. Every code sample on https://chatwarden.dev/ is copied from these READMEs.

## Adopt fast

In your project folder, run `npm install @chatwarden/http @chatwarden/core`, then `npx chatwarden init`. With nothing installed yet, `npx -p @chatwarden/http chatwarden init` runs the same command. It asks only what it cannot detect, then writes the kit (engine, store and matcher), the mount for Express, Fastify, Next.js route handlers or anything on Web `Request` and `Response` (`toFetch`), three starter hooks and a synthetic term pack. It can also write the chat box, the moderator hub and a Discord feed. It never overwrites a file and never writes a secret. The starter hooks carry `TODO(auth)`, `TODO(identity)` and `TODO(terms)` markers, and `npx chatwarden init --check` lists what is left. A game server in another language uses the service API instead: `@chatwarden/http/service` is a `/v1` API over the kit, `chatwarden serve` runs it as a process and `chatwarden init --service` writes a Docker recipe folder.

- [Recipe: Express](https://github.com/hainix/chatwarden/blob/main/docs/recipes/express.md): the files init writes for an Express server, and the one line you add.
- [Recipe: Fastify](https://github.com/hainix/chatwarden/blob/main/docs/recipes/fastify.md): the files init writes for a Fastify server.
- [Recipe: Next.js](https://github.com/hainix/chatwarden/blob/main/docs/recipes/nextjs.md): the route handlers init writes for Next.js, and how any server on Web `Request` uses them.
- [Recipe: Socket.IO](https://github.com/hainix/chatwarden/blob/main/docs/recipes/socketio.md): the chat box on a Socket.IO server, with every line still going through the chat check.
- [Recipe: Colyseus](https://github.com/hainix/chatwarden/blob/main/docs/recipes/colyseus.md): a recipe written by hand for a Colyseus room; init does not write it.
- [Recipe: Urgent reports and welfare](https://github.com/hainix/chatwarden/blob/main/docs/recipes/urgent-and-welfare.md): the urgent lane, the welfare reason, and what the kit does and does not do about a player in trouble.
- [Recipe: Rooms under attack](https://github.com/hainix/chatwarden/blob/main/docs/recipes/raids.md): lock a room, start an emergency, take lines back, and probation for new accounts.
- [Recipe: The weekly digest](https://github.com/hainix/chatwarden/blob/main/docs/recipes/digest.md): Insights and the digest you send from your own timer.
- [Recipe: Rooms for children](https://github.com/hainix/chatwarden/blob/main/docs/recipes/kids-rooms.md): a stricter context for a room, phrase-only chat and blocks.
- [Recipe: Creator channels](https://github.com/hainix/chatwarden/blob/main/docs/recipes/creator-channels.md): staff scope, so a creator's moderators see only that creator's rooms.
- [Recipe: Service mode](https://github.com/hainix/chatwarden/blob/main/docs/recipes/service-mode.md): the `/v1` service API for a game server in any language, with the Docker recipe.
- [Recipe: Translations](https://github.com/hainix/chatwarden/blob/main/docs/recipes/translations.md): the Spanish and Portuguese catalogues, which are machine drafts, and how to add a language.
- [Recipe: Appeal links and emails](https://github.com/hainix/chatwarden/blob/main/docs/recipes/appeal-emails.md): the signed appeal link, the page it opens, the `notices.deliver` hook that mails it, and the signed delivery webhook for service mode.

## What is in it

Everything below is optional. The names are settled at 0.2.0, except that the Discord bot, Coop and EOS integrations are experimental: they were written from the services' documents and have not run against the live services.

- Chat box: for a game with no chat, `<ChatBox>` from `@chatwarden/player-react/chat` is a moderated chat for one room, served by `createRoomBroadcaster` and `chatRoutes` in `@chatwarden/http`.
- Pacing: slow mode, a burst limit and a repeat limit for each room and player, off until you set them. Signals are facts your game records about a player, shown where a profile rule says so; a signal never acts on its own.
- Appeal links and the landing page (0.2.1): a sanction notice can carry a signed link to a page the kit serves (`GET /appeal` and `/appeal/case`, with `CHATWARDEN_PUBLIC_URL` in `chatwarden serve`), where the player reads what happened and files one appeal without signing in; `@chatwarden/player-react/appeal` has the same page as `AppealPage` for a page of your own, with its words from `@chatwarden/core/notice-locales`. The `notices.deliver` hook (or the signed delivery webhook in service mode) hands the notice and the appeal outcome to your own mail system; the kit never sends email. A moderator picks one of nine fixed reasons, and an overturned appeal sets the strikes aside and flags the term, filter and reporter numbers. Off until you set `landingUrl` and turn appeals on.
- Moderation principles, team notes and a recommended setup (0.2.2): the team writes its principles as a list it controls (name, what it covers, examples, outcome, which levels each covers), keeps staff-only team notes tied to a Community Rule and edits the standard the AI is given; the AI read and the guide use them. The owner's first-run panel and `chatwarden init --game competitive|social|kids|creator` start from a recommendation. A report about play or a name (leaving, cheating, an offensive name) is worded and filled in for what it is, not as chat, and the AI reads chat only. `retention.subjectsMs` removes the identity rows of a person with no record after 400 days.
- Email for automatic timeouts is an option (0.2.3): `notices.deliverAutomatic` (default on; `CHATWARDEN_DELIVER_AUTOMATIC` in `chatwarden serve`). Set it to false and the delivery hook is not called for the kit's own automatic chat restrictions; a moderator's sanction and every appeal outcome are still delivered.
- Appeals and names: a player can ask for a second look at a sanction (off until you turn it on), and a moderator decides. A name check can keep a blocked name as evidence and ask a player for a new name; the hub hides names the word list flags until shown.
- AI help: off until you give it an adapter. It reads each report after the player has been told it arrived and shows what it found. At level 2 it pre-fills a mild suggestion that a moderator accepts or edits. It never writes a sanction, a strike, a mute or a notice: it never acts on its own yet.
- AI gate dashboard and shadow mode: a read-only table in the hub shows the numbers that would decide whether the AI may act. Shadow mode lets it decide what it would have done and records that in a table of its own; nothing is written to a player.
- Community term list: a loader for a signed, versioned list that servers can opt in to (`@chatwarden/matcher/corpus`). The package ships no terms and nothing is on by default.
- Integrations: a Discord bot for lookups and, after a confirm step, decisions (`@chatwarden/http/discord`); Coop review jobs (`@chatwarden/http/coop`); Epic Online Services sanctions and reports (`@chatwarden/http/eos`).
- Urgent desk and welfare: a report is urgent from its reason or when a moderator marks it; urgent cases sort first and a moderator can note that the case was passed to the game's safety team. The kit decides nothing and contacts no one (`desk`, `safety` and `rooms` profile sections).
- Second look and Insights: staff comments and escalation (`desk.workflow`), and team numbers with an optional digest (`desk.insights`, `cw.insights`). Both are off until you turn them on.
- Rooms under attack: lock a room or start an emergency (`cw.rooms.setMode`, always expiring), take lines back for everyone, probation for new accounts and a report-surge hint.
- Chat filters: links, personal information, phrases, and caps, repeats, emoji and mentions, each with an action and a Community Rule, with a test box and a dry run in the hub. Off until set.
- Privacy requests and legal hold: `cw.privacy` finds, exports and erases one person's data, and `cw.legal` holds a report with a signed evidence bundle; the owner's routes and the hub's "Data requests" screen use them. It describes what the kit stores and is not legal advice.
- Contexts and staff scope: rules per room (`profile.contexts`), and staff who see only some rooms (`scope`), default-deny, with limited sanctions.
- Blocks and phrase-only chat: a two-way block (`cw.blocks`), and rooms where players pick from phrases you declare (`cw.chat.acceptPhrase`).
- Reserved names: `names.reserved` keeps names such as staff titles for you; a report, a name check and a rename can be about an entity (a clan, guild or team). Terms without spaces: matching for Chinese, Japanese, Thai, Lao, Khmer and Burmese.
- Service mode and shared pacing: `@chatwarden/http/service` (service keys, rate limits, idempotency, an OpenAPI description, `createServiceClient`), `chatwarden serve`, and `createChatwarden({ sharedPacing: true })` so several processes judge one player's lines together.
- Spanish and Portuguese: `@chatwarden/player-react/locales/es` and `/pt`, `@chatwarden/hub-react/locales/es` and `/pt`. They are machine drafts and no person has read them: have a native speaker read the notice and refusal words first. The shared notice words are in `@chatwarden/core/notice-copy`.
- Test kit: `@chatwarden/store-memory/testing` has a fake clock and a scripted chat simulator to test your own rules, for tests only.

## Docs (README per package)

- [Repository README](https://github.com/hainix/chatwarden/blob/main/README.md): what the kit is, the package list and which packages to install for which job.
- [@chatwarden/core](https://github.com/hainix/chatwarden/blob/main/packages/core/README.md): the moderation engine (chat verdicts, reports, decisions, notices, pacing, appeals, the optional AI); no runtime dependencies. Start here.
- [@chatwarden/matcher](https://github.com/hainix/chatwarden/blob/main/packages/matcher/README.md): the slur matcher that resists Unicode and leetspeak evasion without blocking innocent words, and the loader for the community term list; includes invented test words.
- [@chatwarden/store-sqlite](https://github.com/hainix/chatwarden/blob/main/packages/store-sqlite/README.md): the SQLite store for reports, sanctions, notices and the audit trail, on the SQLite built into Node.
- [@chatwarden/store-memory](https://github.com/hainix/chatwarden/blob/main/packages/store-memory/README.md): an in-memory store for tests, demos and single-process prototypes, with a test kit; everything is lost on restart.
- [@chatwarden/http](https://github.com/hainix/chatwarden/blob/main/packages/http/README.md): HTTP routes for staff and players, signed webhooks, Express and Web fetch adapters, the `chatwarden init` command, chat routes, and the Discord bot, Coop and EOS integrations.
- [@chatwarden/profanity](https://github.com/hainix/chatwarden/blob/main/packages/profanity/README.md): an optional filter for ordinary swearing that a game can allow, star or block.
- [@chatwarden/discord](https://github.com/hainix/chatwarden/blob/main/packages/discord/README.md): posts the staff review queue into a Discord forum through a channel webhook.
- [@chatwarden/hub-react](https://github.com/hainix/chatwarden/blob/main/packages/hub-react/README.md): the moderator hub, a React workbench for a team of moderators with one case per player by default, editable steps and reporting, over the staff routes; adopt it as a drop-in `<Hub>`, as pieces, as hooks or headless.
- [@chatwarden/player-react](https://github.com/hainix/chatwarden/blob/main/packages/player-react/README.md): the player side, React components for notices, a player's record, the rules and a report dialog (one step by default), and the moderated chat box.
- [@chatwarden/hub-element](https://github.com/hainix/chatwarden/blob/main/packages/hub-element/README.md): the moderator hub as one custom element, `<chatwarden-hub>`, in a single script tag with no React or build step on the page.
- [Community term list](https://github.com/hainix/chatwarden/blob/main/docs/community-list.md): how a moderator suggests a word, and the rules for what the list accepts.

## npm packages

- [@chatwarden/core on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@chatwarden/core): the engine; install this first.
- [@chatwarden/matcher on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@chatwarden/matcher): the slur matcher.
- [@chatwarden/store-sqlite on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@chatwarden/store-sqlite): the SQLite store.
- [@chatwarden/store-memory on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@chatwarden/store-memory): the in-memory store and test kit.
- [@chatwarden/http on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@chatwarden/http): the HTTP routes, adapters and the `chatwarden` command.
- [@chatwarden/profanity on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@chatwarden/profanity): the optional profanity filter.
- [@chatwarden/discord on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@chatwarden/discord): the Discord review-queue feed.
- [@chatwarden/hub-react on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@chatwarden/hub-react): the moderator hub for React.
- [@chatwarden/player-react on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@chatwarden/player-react): the player notices, report dialog and chat box for React.
- [@chatwarden/hub-element on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@chatwarden/hub-element): the moderator hub as `<chatwarden-hub>`.

## Optional

- [Source repository](https://github.com/hainix/chatwarden): the code, issues and pull requests.
